Native Adventure compass site popup text grammar (53.16 PE)

Source images come from data/runtime/native-pe-images.json. This document is
a reconstruction of native source branches requested for the translation
task; it is not a test or a report of observed in-game output.

Steam image:   PE:6a70a6d9:02711000
Classic image: PE:6a70b91c:0270a000

All addresses below are RVAs.

Role                               Steam               Classic
Owning adventure renderer          7f3cb0..7f6c21      7f1530..7f44a1
Cached compass site popup          7f5490..7f5837      7f2d10..7f30b7
Site kind leaf                     10cbe50..10cc160    10c6dc0..10c70d0
Site kind 11-way table              10cc160             10c70d0
Site dark adjective                10cbe10             10c6d80
Creature raw NAME[2] adjective      aa3770              aa07f0
Native language site name          a946e0              a91760
Site squared distance              1083120             107e090
Site bearing                       1083220             107e190
Popup bearing 16-way table          7f6ba0              7f4420
Complete popup string -> wrap      8e7310              8e4b80

Popup producer (same branch order in both configured images)

    site = lookup_site(selected_compass_site_id);
    if (!site || !controlled_unit) leave_popup_branch;
    text = "The ";
    if (site.type == 1) text += "dark ";
    if (site.type != 10) {
        entity = governing_entity_for_site(site);
        if (entity && !(entity.flags & 0x400)) {
            text += creature_raw[entity.race].name[2];
            text += ' ';
        }
    }
    text += site_kind(site);
    if (site.name.has_name) {
        text += " of ";
        text += native_language_name(site.name, capitalize=true,
                                     only_first_part=false);
    }
    text += (site.type == 3 && site.max_depth == 0) ? " are " : " is ";
    bearing = site_bearing(site, player_position);
    if (bearing == -1 || currently_in_selected_site(site, player_position)) {
        text += "here";
    } else {
        d = site_squared_xy_distance(site, player_position);
        if (d > 100)     text += "far";
        else if (d >=64) text += "a day's travel";
        else if (d >=36) text += "nearly a day's travel";
        else if (d >=9)  text += "a half day's travel";
        else if (d >=0)  text += "a short walk";
        // Signed-negative result appends no distance words.
        text += " to the ";
        text += compass_bearing[bearing];
    }
    text += ".";
    wrap_complete_string(text, width=30);

The currently_in_selected_site branch is the native conjunction recovered
from Steam 7f5660..7f56cd / Classic 7f2ee0..7f2f4d:

    current_site != null;
    current_site has no absolute subsite coordinate
        (subtype data absent or subtype+0x20 == 0xfff0bdc0);
    current_site == selected_site;
    either tile-location flags contain 0x100 or no current-site-building
        was returned by the local-coordinate lookup.

The 16 bearing outputs, ordered by both native jump tables, are exactly:

    north, north-northeast, northeast, east-northeast,
    east, east-southeast, southeast, south-southeast,
    south, south-southwest, southwest, west-southwest,
    west, west-northwest, northwest, north-northwest.

The bearing getter's complete body returns only -1 or 0..15. It uses the
site's absolute subsite coordinate when available and otherwise the site
rectangle's center; coincident XY returns -1, other XY follows the native
atan2 and 16 angular interval branches. Therefore the caller's >15 default
does not introduce another normally reachable bearing production.

The distance getter uses the same subsite-or-site-center alternatives and
returns the sum of squared XY offsets in the native signed 32-bit result.
Its fallback branch follows the first return and is retained in the source
disassembly through the beginning of the adjacent bearing helper. Negative
distance is still retained as the caller's native branch; it has no words.

There are 97 finite where productions including final punctuation:

    "here."
    five distance phrases x 16 bearings
    empty distance x 16 bearings

The empty-distance forms append the literal leading space from " to the ".
Since agreement already ends in a space, the unwrapped native sentence has
two spaces in " is  to the " or " are  to the ". A native word-wrap boundary
can consume one of the physical separator spaces. This is a producer branch,
not an invented fragment for the supplied screenshot.

Site-kind leaf: complete selector and subtype branches

    type 0 or 3:
        min_depth == 0 && max_depth > 0 -> "fortress"
        min_depth > 0                 -> "mountain halls"
        other depth values            -> "hillocks"
    type 1:
        IS_CITY (flags[0] & 8)        -> "fortress"
        otherwise                     -> "pits"
    type 2                            -> "cave"
    type 4                            -> "forest retreat"
    type 5:
        IS_CITY                       -> "town"
        otherwise                     -> "hamlet"
    type 6                            -> "important location"
    type 7:
        lair subtype == 3             -> "shrine"
        lair subtype == 2             -> "labyrinth"
        other/missing subtype         -> "lair"
    type 8:
        missing subtype               -> "fortress"
        fortress subtype == 1         -> "tower"
        fortress subtype == 2         -> "monastery"
        fortress subtype == 3         -> "fort"
        other subtype                 -> "castle"
    type 9                            -> "camp"
    type 10:
        monument subtype == 0         -> "tomb"
        monument subtype == 1         -> "vault"
        monument subtype == 2:
            size >= 100               -> "mysterious palace"
            15 <= size < 100           -> "mysterious dungeon"
            size < 15                 -> "mysterious lair"
        other/missing subtype         -> "monument"
    other type                        -> "site"

These are the same 24 distinct site nouns and dark/race composition recorded
by data/extracted/world-site-type-sources.tsv and already handled by the
existing world_site_type resolver. No additional site kind is inferred from
the screenshot's word "lair".

The creature field is the RAW adjective NAME[2], not the singular or plural
species name. The popup sets caste=-1, so the helper reads creature_raw+0x60;
the helper's optional caste fallback is retained in the disassembly but is
not selected by this popup. The source remains a complete semantic field,
including installed or mod-provided creature adjectives.

Native site names are open data, not a finite English literal set. The saved
language formatter includes authored first names, nickname policies, native
language words, compound parts, articles and "of" names. It is the existing
native site-name field handled by the name resolver; it must not be split
into generic dictionary tokens or hardcoded to "Ashencavern".

The four complete sentence shells are:

    The {site-description} of {site-name} is {where}.
    The {site-description} of {site-name} are {where}.
    The {site-description} is {where}.
    The {site-description} are {where}.

The screenshot uses the named singular shell, the site kind "lair", native
site name "Ashencavern", the >100 distance band and bearing case 2.

Scope of the adjacent compass listing and other map cards

The left compass frame is a site list, not a separate creature/quest popup.
Its native listing literals, 16 abbreviated bearings, Gui/Qst badges and ***
marker are also retained in the saved listing block and switch inventory.
Gui is the category-2 guide badge; Qst is the category-1 quest badge; *** is
the current-site/unknown-bearing marker. Each hovered list row writes that
same site's +0x88 id to the cached popup selector. Neither badge introduces
another right-popup prose branch.

The complete owning Adventure renderer is retained, including the separate
map look-info and Track/Spoor cards. Those are different native popup paths
and have their existing map-hover/tracking semantic owners. In the compass
site block, a failed site lookup leaves the branch; there is no alternative
quest, unit, creature, location category, or warning text to enumerate there.

Inventory files

    native-owners.tsv: complete selected native bodies and lexical blocks
    native-literals.tsv: exact RIP and inline operands, with instruction RVAs
    native-calls.tsv: direct calls/tail calls from each retained body
    native-switches.tsv: raw PE jump-table entries, not a hand-counted list
    native-components.tsv: popup/type/list operands and bearing case sources
    native-productions.tsv: dynamic sentence fields and finite where grammar
    steam-producer-and-helpers.asm / classic-producer-and-helpers.asm:
        owning renderer, popup, all semantic text helpers and listing block

The extractor only reads configured image files and writes these native
source inventories. No game UI, runtime load state, build, translation
generator, self-test or simulated in-game display was used.
